name: mkldnn_max_pool3d
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI): aten::mkldnn_max_pool3d(Tensor self, int[3] kernel_size, int[3] stride=[], int[3] padding=0, int[3] dilation=1, bool ceil_mode=False) -> Tensor. This representative signature is NOT exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract, including overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and must never be narrowed to this one signature. Registered schemas (verbatim): aten::mkldnn_max_pool3d(Tensor self, int[3] kernel_size, int[3] stride=[], int[3] padding=0, int[3] dilation=1, bool ceil_mode=False) -> Tensor ; aten::mkldnn_max_pool3d.out(Tensor self, int[3] kernel_size, int[3] stride=[], int[3] padding=0, int[3] dilation=1, bool ceil_mode=False, *, Tensor(a!) out) -> Tensor(a!). Semantics: 3-D max pooling over a rank-5 NCDHW MkldnnCPU blocking-layout tensor; kernel_size/stride/padding/dilation are int[3] lists expanded to the rank (rank-4 inputs and 2-element lists are refused at runtime), padding is zero by default, dilation must be 1, both ceil_mode settings are exercised against the reference, and pooling copies stored values so results compare exactly. The schema's JSON defaults are retained as rendered: stride=[] is the native empty-list default form (the pytest notes an empty stride list as the documented default), while padding=0 and dilation=1 are integer scalars the schema broadcasts to the int[3] list defaults [0,0,0] and [1,1,1]. Overload-dependent behavior stays in pytest: the out= overload is keyword-only, aliases and returns the provided buffer, and mutates it; the default overload allocates and returns a fresh Tensor, so this definition's mutates/returns_alias_of describe only the representative default overload.
